messages:
Vendor Oncall: Hey Redwood team, quick heads-up: our monitoring flagged a developer debug job that accidentally logged partial AWS access keys to an S3 bucket under our account around 2026-03-19T22:10Z. We're investigating scope. :eyes:
Marta (SecEng): Thanks for the ping. Can you confirm which bucket and whether those objects are public? Also do you use customer-managed CMKs or vendor-managed keys for those objects?
Vendor Oncall: Bucket: vendor-logs-prod-us-west-2, objects in prefix debug/2026-03-19/. Not public ACLs, but lifecycle allowed read by our ops role. We use our AWS-managed keys (not CMK).
Alex (VendorSRE): Understood. Immediate ask: rotate any IAM keys that were logged and revoke active sessions tied to them. Can you share the last 6 characters of the key so we can correlate in CloudTrail?
Vendor Oncall: Last 6 chars: AB9x3F. Rotating now. We've kicked the service principal and started rotation.
Chloe (Infra): From our side, please provide a signed statement that vendor will not read customer-owned buckets or KMS keys. Also, did the logs include any customer identifiers (org IDs, bucket names, token prefixes)?
Vendor Oncall: We don't see customer bucket names in the snippet, only service internal identifiers and stack traces. We're running a grep across the full prefix to confirm.
Marta (SecEng): Action plan: 1) Contain (rotate/revoke) 2) Full grep of the log prefix for any customer PII or secret-like strings 3) Provide CloudTrail query output for any GetObject/HeadObject calls in that prefix 4) Provide commit/ticket showing why debug job wrote keys 5) Publish timeline + remediation.
security-bot: Automated alert: related CloudTrail events for IAM:ListAccessKeys and STS:AssumeRole were seen within window 2026-03-19T21:50Z-22:20Z. See internal link: https://siem.internal/alerts/INC-3221
Alex (VendorSRE): Sharing quick CloudTrail query to help:
```
aws cloudtrail lookup-events --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=EventName,AttributeValue=GetObject --start-time 2026-03-19T21:00:00Z --end-time 2026-03-19T23:00:00Z --query 'Events[*].{Time:EventTime,User:Username,Resource:Resources}'
```
Vendor Oncall: Ran grep, found 12 files with partial key strings; none reference customer IDs. We've rotated credentials and will push new versions. Uploading grep results to shared drive now: https://files.vendor/incident/1782398642/report.txt
Marta (SecEng): Good. Next: we need the S3 object inventory and ACLs snapshot and an export of any KMS Decrypt/GenerateDataKey events (if any) tied to the service role. Even if you used AWS-managed keys, we need assurance there was no cross-account decrypt.
Chloe (Infra): For our audit trail, we'll run a cross-account CloudTrail search for any foreign Principal accessing our buckets in that time range. If anything shows, we'll escalate.
Vendor Oncall: Confirmed no cross-account access from vendor to Redwood buckets. No Decrypt events for customer CMKs.
Marta (SecEng): OK. Communications: We'll treat this as a moderate third-party exposure. Legal and Trust will draft a customer notification template if we find any customer data in those logs. For now, prepare a short joint statement: what happened, scope (no customer data found so far), actions taken, and next steps.
Alex (VendorSRE): Also suggestion: temporarily narrow the vendor role's RBAC to remove s3:GetObject on non-essential prefixes while you finish the audit. Apply least privilege for 48h.
Vendor Oncall: Applying RBAC restriction now. Noted.
ops-notify-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-1782398642, severity: medium. Pager duty oncall: @chloe. Postmortem owner: Marta.
Marta (SecEng): We'll run a round of retrospective checks: ensure vendor logs are scanned for secrets (regex rules), require use of CMKs next quarter for sensitive logs, and add a contract clause for mandatory key rotation in 24h after any detected leakage.
Vendor Oncall: Thanks — we'll share formal timeline and the grep artifacts by EOD. Apologies on our side, this was an internal debug flag left on during a deploy.
Marta (SecEng): Appreciated. Follow-ups: 1) upload sanitized artifacts to secure folder, 2) rotate any remaining credentials, 3) schedule 1:1 post-incident sync tomorrow 09:00 PT. If any customer indicators appear, escalate immediately. :lock:
Alex (VendorSRE): +1 on post-incident sync. I'll join and bring the rotation logs.
Vendor Oncall: Confirmed 09:00 PT. Closing thread for now, will update when artifacts uploaded. :white_check_mark:
